schindler-s-list.gazette: Schindler's lists survive as documents — typed names, work classifications, transfers to the Brünnlitz plant in occupied Czechoslovakia — and the roughly 1,100 people on them have left descendants now numbering in the thousands. Spielberg shot in Kraków, blocks from the ghetto cleared in March 1943, and was refused permission to film inside Auschwitz, so the camp material was staged outside the gates looking out. The closing sequence brings actual Schindlerjuden to the grave on Mount Zion, each laying a stone.

clerks-1994.gazette: Kevin Smith worked days behind the counter at the Quick Stop in Leonardo, New Jersey, and shot the film there at night, after the store closed. The shutters stayed down for the entire shoot, which is why the script has someone gum up the locks. The budget came to about $27,575, raised on credit cards and a sold comic collection, and the counter talk came off the shift Smith was still working.

hamnet-2025.gazette: Hamnet Shakespeare was buried at Holy Trinity in Stratford in August 1596, aged eleven; the parish register gives the burial and no cause. English plague medicine of the period ran on vinegar, herb bundles and sealed houses, and London's theatres closed by order whenever the death bills rose. Hamlet reached the Globe around 1600, four years after that burial, in a period when Stratford scribes wrote the two names interchangeably.
hamnet-2025.prism: The craft here is mostly filling silence — the documents hand over a burial line and a playhouse, and the sickroom, the medicine and the marriage all have to be built from nothing. That isn't a weakness in the film so much as the shape of what survives about ordinary Elizabethan households, which is almost none of it.

forrest-gump-1994.gazette: ILM composited Tom Hanks into news footage of Kennedy, Johnson and Nixon, reanimating archival mouths frame by frame so the presidents delivered new lines. George Wallace's stand in the schoolhouse door at the University of Alabama in June 1963 is real footage; the student handed a dropped book is not. The work took the visual-effects Oscar and set the terms for a decade of archival compositing.

hoop-dreams-1994.gazette: The shoot began in 1987 as a half-hour PBS short about playground basketball and ran five years, some 250 hours of tape, following William Gates and Arthur Agee from Chicago courts to St. Joseph High School in suburban Westchester, Illinois. Neither player reached the NBA; Agee's father, who appears throughout, was murdered in 2004. When the documentary branch left the film off its 1995 shortlist, the Academy rewrote its nomination rules.

pom-poko-1994.gazette: Tama New Town rose in the hills west of Tokyo from the mid-1960s, one of the largest planned developments in Japan: ridgelines cut, valleys filled, the resident raccoon dogs pushed off their range. Takahata's narrator reports it the way a broadcaster would, in dates, phases and casualty figures, while the tanuki answer with shapeshifting and folklore. Raccoon dogs still live in the Tokyo suburbs, mostly noticed when they are hit by cars.
pom-poko-1994.prism: The tanuki who can hold a human shape end up in suits, commuting; the ones who can't are simply gone. The film's verdict on development isn't that it killed them — it's that it absorbed the ones it could use.

the-blue-kite-1994.gazette: The Anti-Rightist Campaign of 1957 ran partly on quotas, with work units expected to produce a share of rightists and names found to fill the number. Tian Zhuangzhuang's film tracks a single Beijing household through that campaign, the famine that followed the Great Leap Forward, and the Cultural Revolution, marking each by the loss of a father. Chinese authorities banned the film and barred Tian from directing; he did not complete another feature until 2002.

apollo-13-1995.gazette: The Apollo 13 air-to-ground transcripts are public, and what the crew said on 13 April 1970 was 'Houston, we've had a problem.' 'Failure is not an option' appears nowhere in them — the line was written for the 1995 screenplay, and flight director Gene Kranz later took it as the title of his memoir. It now circulates as something spoken in mission control.

casino-1995.gazette: The Stardust skim worked before the count: cash lifted from the counting room and carried to Chicago, Kansas City and Milwaukee, until FBI wiretaps produced the Strawman prosecutions that put those bosses away in the mid-1980s. Frank Rosenthal survived a car bomb in a Las Vegas parking lot in 1982; Tony Spilotro and his brother were beaten to death and buried in an Indiana cornfield in 1986. The Stardust itself lasted until 2007, when it was imploded to clear the lot.
casino-1995.prism: The skim ran on men who could be trusted with cash nobody wrote down. What replaced them was a compliance department — the indictments cleared the room, and the public companies made sure it stayed cleared.

crumb-1995.gazette: Charles Crumb had not left his mother's house in Philadelphia for years when Terry Zwigoff began filming; Maxon lived in a San Francisco residential hotel and sat on a bed of nails. Robert had already traded a stack of sketchbooks for a house in southern France. Charles died by suicide in 1992, before the film was released; it carries a dedication to him.

city-of-god-2002.gazette: Cidade de Deus was built by the Rio state government in the 1960s to move favela residents out of the South Zone, and it remains a real address west of the city. Paulo Lins grew up there and spent roughly eight years on the research, much of it as an assistant on an anthropological study of local violence, before it became a novel. The film was cast largely out of Rio's favelas through an acting workshop, most of the young leads with no screen experience at all.

fahrenheit-9-11-2004.gazette: Disney blocked Miramax from releasing the film in May 2004; it went out through Lions Gate and IFC and became the highest-grossing documentary ever made. It took the Palme d'Or at Cannes that same month and opened in American theatres in June, four months before the election it was arguing about. Bush won that election by roughly three million votes.
fahrenheit-9-11-2004.prism: Record box office and a lost election in the same calendar year — that's the ceiling on the form, stated plainly. A documentary can reach more people than any before it and still mostly reach the ones already convinced.

munich-2005.gazette: Eleven members of the Israeli Olympic team were killed on 5 September 1972, most of them during the failed rescue attempt at the Fürstenfeldbruck airfield. Israel's response, the operation known as Wrath of God, included a 1973 killing in Lillehammer that hit the wrong man — a Moroccan waiter, Ahmed Bouchikhi — for which Israel paid his family compensation in 1996 without admitting responsibility. Spielberg built his account from George Jonas's Vengeance, a book whose central source former Israeli intelligence officers have disputed since publication.

paradise-now-2005.gazette: Nablus in 2004 was under regular Israeli incursion, and Hany Abu-Assad shot there anyway. A missile struck near the set, the location manager was abducted and later released, and part of the crew walked; the remaining scenes were finished in Nazareth. When the film took the Golden Globe in January 2006, the presenter announced it as coming from Palestine, and the wording became its own news story.

letters-from-iwo-jima-2006.gazette: Tadamichi Kuribayashi commanded the Iwo Jima garrison and wrote home constantly, letters later published in Japan alongside the small drawings he made for his son. He had spent two years in the United States as a junior officer in the late 1920s and told his family the Americans were the last people Japan should fight. The battle ran from 19 February to 26 March 1945; his body was never identified, and Japanese recovery teams are still working the island's tunnels.
letters-from-iwo-jima-2006.prism: The letters anyone can read are the ones that got off the island. The men who wrote the rest are still being pulled out of the rock eight decades later, which is the part no reconstruction can stage.
